- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (sentiment = 0.00 or negative), model tends to overreact; apply downward bias correction of 0.5–1.5% to forecasted values.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% for the following 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows no change (all 0.00), model should not assume momentum; treat as flat market and apply conservative, low-variance forecast adjustments.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the first 10 days of the 30-day horizon; apply a “lag correction” by reducing first 10 forecast values by 0.5–1.5% relative to true outcome.
